{'text': 'Apple today unveiled the M6 chip, the first product in a new generation of chips, and the A20 Pro from the same family will also come to the iPhone 18 Pro. Here are the iPhone 18 Pro performance upgrades the M6 hints at.'}

{'text': 'M6 hints at big performance and efficiency gains for A20 Pro in iPhone 18 Pro'}

{'text': "It's not September yet, but Apple today surprised with two new products: a new Mac mini and Mac Studio. (Order now: Mac mini, Mac Studio.)"}

{'text': "The Mac mini comes with Apple's new-generation M6 chip, from the same family as the A20 Pro that will come to the iPhone 18 Pro."}

{'text': "Here's what the Apple news release says:"}

{'text': '"M6 uses the most advanced 2-nanometer process technology, packing higher transistor density into a smaller chip for a major leap in performance and energy efficiency. M6 also introduces dual 16-core Neural Engines, delivering peak compute that\'s 2x the previous generation, making on-device AI workflows run faster. […] M6 features an all-new 12-core CPU architecture — two more cores than M5 — built from 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores. It delivers the world\'s fastest single-threaded performance, with multi-threaded performance up to 1.2x faster than M5."'}

{'text': "M6 will ultimately be more powerful than the all-new A20 Pro chip in iPhone 18 Pro. That's typically how it works with M chips for Mac and iPad."}

{'text': "But because M6 and A20 Pro are from the same chip family, M6's upgrades are all expected to show up in A20 Pro."}

{'text': 'Most notable among them, A20 Pro will use the new 2-nanometer process Apple has highlighted here, bringing a "major leap in performance and energy efficiency."'}

{'text': 'We had been expecting the jump to 2-nanometer to bring larger gains than usual, and the M6 specs confirm that.'}

{'text': "A20 Pro's CPU and GPU core counts might not be the same as M6, and the dual 16-core Neural Engine is also unknown. But thanks to 2-nanometer, it should bring big improvements in the two areas Apple highlighted today: performance and efficiency."}

{'text': "What will the year-over-year gains actually be? It's too early to say. But when iPhone 18 Pro launches in a few weeks, expect performance and efficiency to be the headline A20 Pro upgrades."}
